extracted.intended_audience: authors and poets (especially debut poets in the UK & Ireland), literary agents, booksellers, rights/permissions enquirers, and general public contacting the publisher
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for submitting debut poetry collections to Picador (Pan Macmillan): eligibility, required manuscript state, submission format, response time, and limits on unsolicited and international submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsolicited submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Pan Macmillan generally doesn’t accept unsolicited manuscripts or proposals. All our submissions come via literary agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information on how to find a literary agent can be found at www.writersandartists.co.uk/writers. This is the publisher-wide policy for unsolicited work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picador Poetry — eligibility (residency and debut status)
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept direct submissions of debut collections from poets resident in the UK and Ireland.*
rubrics_metrics.guidance: *Other submissions, including international, are accepted from agented authors only. We do not accept unsolicited submissions of poetry for children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picador Poetry — manuscript readiness and prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets should have completed a book manuscript and have achieved journal publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an eligibility/quality expectation: completed manuscript plus some journal (periodical) publication history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picador Poetry — submission format and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send an extract of up to 15 pages to picador.poetry@macmillan.com in a single document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a single document containing up to 15 pages; use the provided email address. If the publisher wishes to see more, they will contact you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picador Poetry — response time and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: If we wish to see more of your work, we will contact you within eight weeks. All submitted work will be treated as confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect up to eight weeks for contact if they want more; submissions are treated as confidential per their statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agented submissions for other/ international work
rubrics_metrics.description: Other submissions, including international, are accepted from agented authors only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-UK/Ireland authors and submissions other than debut poetry collections should be agent-represented to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: No unsolicited children's poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not accept unsolicited submissions of poetry for children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Children’s poetry must come via an agent or follow the publisher's separate children’s submission routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential scam warning / verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Fictitious solicitations purporting to be “Letter(s) of Interest,” job openings, and/or requests for payment are occasionally circulated online by individuals posing as Pan Macmillan representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pan Macmillan does not solicit agents, authors, or job candidates in this manner. If in doubt about authenticity, email compliance@macmillan.com before taking action. Pan Macmillan job postings are available online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adult rights and permissions procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to reuse content from Pan Macmillan (adult titles only) please visit https://trade.panmacmillan.com/rights-permissions/permissions and complete the online form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For all adult rights enquiries, email adultrightsquery@macmillan.co.uk. Use the online form or email as directed for reuse permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children's books rights/permissions procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: For requests to use content from Macmillan Children’s Books please follow this link: https://www.panmacmillan.com/childrens-books-permissions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Children’s permissions have a separate process (follow the provided link).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special format requests for students with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: I would like to request a special format of one of your books for a student with disabilities: Please email adultrightsquery@macmillan.co.uk with your request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of the request; use the adult rights query address for accessibility/special-format requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting faults with print titles
rubrics_metrics.description: For print titles, please email details of the problem, as well as author and title details, and ISBN if possible, to faults@macmillan.co.uk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They aim to reply as quickly as possible to all queries, but ask you to allow 28 days before following up on your query.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting faults with ebooks
rubrics_metrics.description: For ebooks, please email details of the problem, as well as author and title details, and the ISBN, to ebooksqueries@macmillan.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide title/author/ISBN and a description of the problem so the ebooks team can investigate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting authors and illustrators (privacy policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are unable to give out our authors' and illustrators' contact details, but we're more than happy to pass messages on to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can email your message to webqueries@macmillan.co.uk or post it to their London address (6 Briset Street, London EC1M 5NR). They cannot guarantee an author response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bookseller order enquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: I am a bookseller and I would like to order books from you: Please email webqueries@macmillan.co.uk with the name of your business and the books you would like to order and we will get back to you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include your business name and the books you want when emailing webqueries@macmillan.co.uk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audiobook enquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: I have a question about one of your audiobooks: Please email audiobooks@macmillan.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct audiobook-specific queries to the audiobooks email address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition queries
rubrics_metrics.description: I have a query about a competition hosted on panmacmillan.com: Please email webqueries@macmillan.co.uk with your question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the general webqueries address for competition-related questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online piracy reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: I would like to report an incident of online piracy of a book, ebook, recording or programme: Please complete the web form at www.panmacmillan.com/piracy-report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The team responds to all reports submitted via the piracy report form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help finding a book — possible reasons and next steps
rubrics_metrics.description: If you can’t find a title that you think we publish it is probably for one of these reasons: -It is out of print -The book’s publication date is more than 5 months away -We don’t publish the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To check the publisher of any book, search Amazon and scroll to the product information section. If the product says Macmillan / Pan / Pan Macmillan / Picador / Tor / Macmillan Children’s Books but you can’t find it on their website, it may be out of print, forthcoming beyond 5 months, or published by Macmillan US (check http://us.macmillan.com/).

rubrics_metrics.name: General Product Safety Regulation compliance and contact
rubrics_metrics.description: All books published by Pan Macmillan comply fully with the requirements of the General Product Safety Regulation (December 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For further information and help with any queries, contact generalproductsafety@macmillan.com, include title and ISBN if possible, and they will respond within 48 hours.
